questions.q: Why fix vmin=-1 and vmax=1 and use a diverging colormap when drawing a correlation heatmap?
options: It speeds up the calculation
Colors then mean the same thing every time, and positive and negative are visually distinct
It removes the diagonal of ones
seaborn refuses to draw the heatmap otherwise
questions.explain: A fixed -1 to 1 scale with a diverging palette centered on zero keeps the colors comparable across charts and shows direction as well as strength.

questions.q: In the illustrative data, Pearson correlation between orders and total_spend was about 0.20 but Spearman was about 0.85. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Spearman always gives larger numbers than Pearson
Orders and total_spend are unrelated
There are missing values in both columns
Two extreme total_spend values distorted Pearson but not the rank-based Spearman
questions.explain: Pearson is sensitive to extreme values. After removing the two huge spend values, Pearson rose to about 0.81, close to Spearman.

questions.q: tenure_months and churned had a correlation of about -0.18. Which reading is best?
options: A weak negative association: longer tenure goes with somewhat less churn
Longer tenure causes customers to stay
Tenure explains 18% of churn exactly
There is no relationship at all
questions.explain: -0.18 is a weak negative association. It says the two move in opposite directions a little, without proving cause.

questions.q: A pair of columns has a Pearson correlation near 0 but the scatter plot shows a clear U shape. What does this illustrate?
options: The data has too many rows
Spearman would also be exactly 1
Pearson correlation only captures linear relationships
U shapes cannot exist in real data
questions.explain: A U-shaped relationship can have near-zero linear correlation. That is why you plot a pair as well as compute the coefficient.

questions.q: Which is the best first response when Pearson and Spearman disagree sharply for a pair of columns?
options: Report whichever number is larger
Delete the column from the dataset
Convert both columns to strings
Plot the pair and check for outliers or a curved relationship
questions.explain: A large gap signals outliers or non-linearity. A scatter plot of the pair shows which, before any number gets reported.
